title: Research Briefing
description: A one-page overview of one research paper for a broad scientific audience, following the Research Briefing format of Nature-family journals.
reference: Structure follows the Research Briefing format that Nature-family journals have used since 2022: a roughly one-page overview that unpacks a paper for a broader scientific audience (https://www.nature.com/articles/s41561-022-01011-3). Word limits follow Nature's Research Briefing author template.

headline.guidance: Different from the paper's title; highlights the key finding; short, catchy, and accessible to non-specialists.

sections.name: This is a summary of
sections.guidance: The paper in Nature citation style: first author et al., title, and DOI and year when printed.

sections.name: The Bio
sections.guidance: The story behind the project, using only what the paper states (motivation, hurdles and how they were solved). This section belongs to the authors: start with 'Draft for the authors:', write in the third person, and never invent personal experiences.

sections.name: The Reason
sections.guidance: The broader scientific problem and why this gap matters to society or other fields, without jargon.

sections.name: The Discovery
sections.guidance: Two short paragraphs: what the authors did, then what they found and how it advances the field. Keep technical terms to a minimum and keep key numbers.

sections.name: The Graphic
sections.guidance: Name the one figure, from the paper's own figure captions, that best shows the main finding, then a standalone caption of about 50 words explaining its takeaway without mentioning panel letters.

sections.name: The Future
sections.guidance: Where the research goes next: open questions and immediate applications the paper points to.

sections.name: Related Reviews and Literature
sections.guidance: Two or three papers or reviews from the paper's reference list (given below) that give the best context for readers, one per bullet, copied as they appear there. Not the paper itself.
